slides.heading: When AI forgets your project
slides.body: A tool called claude-mem is getting attention for a simple idea: make useful context available across coding sessions.

slides.heading: Why it matters
slides.body: A new session can start without the decisions, fixes or failed approaches from the last one. Repeating context costs time.

slides.heading: What the project says
slides.body: Claude-mem says it captures session activity, compresses it with AI and brings relevant context into future sessions.

slides.heading: Try the idea manually
slides.body: Before ending a session, ask: ‘Summarize the goal, decisions, unresolved bugs and next steps. Mark anything uncertain.’ Save the result where you control it.

slides.heading: Memory needs boundaries
slides.body: Check what a tool stores and where it sends data before connecting a project. Don’t put secrets in a handoff. We haven’t tested claude-mem.

caption:
A new AI coding session often means repeating yourself. One approach is to keep a short, reusable handoff of what happened and what comes next.

The claude-mem project describes an automated version of this idea. On October 31, GitHub’s Trending page listed it among the day’s popular repositories. We haven’t installed or tested it, so this isn’t a recommendation or review.

The handoff prompt on slide 4 is our own example. Check any memory tool’s storage, access and privacy settings before use.

What context do you find yourself repeating to AI tools?
